root_cause: Production had already been repaired to use the EU Supavisor transaction pooler, while repository main and the GitHub recovery workflow still contained PostgREST/Data API dependencies. That created runtime/source drift: the live hotfix worked, but a normal redeploy from main could reintroduce the same HTTP 522 failure. Repeated Vault inspection could not close this because the blocked introspection path was not the failing transport.
prevention_rule: Critical content-publication runtime and recovery control-plane code must use the canonical EU Supavisor transaction pooler for internal database access and must not depend on /rest/v1 for scheduler authority or publication-state recovery. Repository source must be reconciled to proven production source before release. Vault values are never introspected as a recovery prerequisite; only bounded authority use and outcome readback are permitted.

database: Direct production SQL succeeded and reported pg_is_in_recovery=false.
The Supabase project remained ACTIVE_HEALTHY in eu-central-1.
failure_domain: PostgREST/Data API requests had returned HTTP 522 during the incident.
The log query backend also returned a backend error while direct SQL remained healthy.
